summary: Commit-seal mismatch quarantines tenant during canary cutover causing transparent fallback and elevated 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
During a canary cutover for rw-vicuna-13b-v2 in us-east, BrightPath experienced a tenant-level quarantine: the tenant's requests were routed to a transparent degraded variant (fallback) and started returning 503/524-like errors from the edge. The event coincided with a staged orchestrator rollout.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: A subset (~0.8% of BrightPath's requests) were silently diverted to the degraded variant for ~22 minutes, causing visible latency increase and a billing spike due to repeated client retries.
- Internal: Alerts for 5xx spike, edge-proxy errors, and quarantine count increase.

Environment:
- Prod | us-east region
- Customer: BrightPath AI (dedicated pool)
- Model: rw-vicuna-13b-v2 pinned for this tenant during canary

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-12 12:02 UTC: Orchestrator rolling update begins for canary slice.
- 2026-03-12 12:04 UTC: BrightPath reports increased latency and occasional 503s.
- 2026-03-12 12:10 UTC: Support opens ticket and escalates to SRE/Orchestrator team.
- 2026-03-12 12:24 UTC: Engineering identifies a commit-seal propagation mismatch related to snapshot re-sequencing.
- 2026-03-12 12:34 UTC: Manual quarantine clear + edge proxy restart applied; traffic returns to expected variant.
- 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC: Hotfix merged to orchestrator repro sequence; patch rollout scheduled.

Steps to reproduce (internal / dev repro):
1) Deploy canary variant with orchestrator snapshot re-sequencing enabled (feature flag ff/orch/snapshot-skip=false).
2) Issue commit that intentionally delays seal write by 1-5s (simulated in test harness).
3) Trigger tenant pin commit while prewarm and health probes overlap with the delayed seal write.
4) Observe tenant quarantine counter increment and routing to degraded variant.

Observed behaviour:
- Tenant record enters quarantine due to commit-seal mismatch: orchestrator snapshot marks the tenant as not fully committed while the edge still sees a pin.
- Edge routing policy detects inconsistency and, per quarantine policy, routes traffic to fallback variant to avoid serving an uncommitted model.
- Requests from the tenant saw increased tail latency and some 5xx from edge-proxy while quarantine persisted.

Expected behaviour:
- Orchestrator should guarantee commit-seal atomicity for tenant pins across snapshot propagation during a rolling update; quarantine should not trigger when pin commit is present and prewarm completes.

Relevant logs (snippets):
- orchestrator@12:04:09 UTC INFO commit: starting commit for tenant=brightpath-42 snapshot=2026-03-12T12:04:09Z
- orchestrator@12:04:11 UTC WARN seal-write-delay: write took 4.1s tenant=brightpath-42
- edge-proxy@12:04:13 UTC ERROR routing: quarantine-triggered tenant=brightpath-42 reason=commit-seal-mismatch
- edge-proxy@12:04:13 UTC ERROR http: upstream 503 for tenant=brightpath-42 path=/v1/generate

Initial hypothesis:
- A race between snapshot application and seal write acknowledgement left the control-plane with an inconsistent view: orchestrator considered the commit incomplete while the edge had a transient version pin. Quarantine logic is aggressive and opted to divert to fallback.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Manually issued admin command clear_quarantine(tenant=brightpath-42) to force reconciler to re-evaluate pinned version.
- Restarted edge-proxy pod handling brightpath slice to flush stale local routing cache.
- Temporarily disabled orchestrator feature flag ff/orch/snapshot-resque to prevent new snapshots from using the problematic path during investigation.

Follow-up / permanent fix planned:
- Hotfix to orchestrator to ensure commit-seal writes are sequenced before snapshot visibility (PR linked).
- Add a 2s tolerant window in edge quarantine logic to reduce sensitivity to transient seal latency for pinned tenants.
- Add more telemetry: instrument seal-write latency histogram and quarantine cause tags for easier alerting.

Notes on customer communication:
- BrightPath notified at 12:18 UTC that we were investigating and provided ETA for a mitigation.
- Post-incident summary and billing impact assessment will be shared by 2026-03-16.

investigation_notes: Seal-write latency spikes were correlated with increased snapshot churn during orchestrator rolling update.
Quarantine logic currently has zero tolerance for commit-seal mismatch for pinned tenants; triggers immediate fallback to degraded variant.
Reproducer harness confirmed that artificially delaying seal writes by >2s can trigger quarantine during overlapping prewarm/healthcheck windows.
Telemetry did not previously expose per-tenant seal-write histograms; we will add that in follow-up.
No indications of GPU capacity exhaustion or serving-runtime errors; the issue is control-plane sequencing and edge policy sensitivity.
resolution_notes: Mitigation: Executed admin clear_quarantine for tenant brightpath-42 and restarted the edge-proxy slice handling the tenant to flush routing cache.
Fix: Merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4128 to enforce pre-seal snapshot visibility and to retry seal-write with backoff on transient latency.
Policy change: Added a conservative 2s tolerant window to edge quarantine logic to avoid transient misroutes for pinned tenants; will iterate on threshold after telemetry.
Monitoring: Added alert rule for seal-write-latency>1s per-slice and quarantine-count>0 for pinned-tenant to #support and #sre-alerts.
Customer remediation: Offered credit for requests affected; finance will follow up.

Add per-tenant seal-write histogram and quarantine cause tags to telemetry within two sprints.
Adjust quarantine sensitivity thresholds after 48h of hotfix telemetry and update runbook accordingly.
Finance to complete billing impact assessment and coordinate customer credit by 2026-03-16.
